description: State and locality salary/labor law transparency requirements. Source of truth for ST-* rules.

CA.name: California
CA.notes: Pay range required in ALL job postings, including remote roles that could be performed in CA. Benefits summary not required but recommended.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.law: CO SB21-085 (Equal Pay for Equal Work Act)
CO.notes: Pay range AND benefits summary required. Applies to all remote roles that can be performed in CO. 'Nationwide except CO' exclusions are no longer compliant as of 2022.

NY.name: New York
NY.notes: Pay range required for jobs to be performed in NY or where the employer reasonably expects the applicant pool to include NY residents.

NYC.name: New York City
NYC.notes: NYC enacted pay transparency earlier than the state. Same standard applies.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: Pay range AND general benefits description required for postings with 15+ employees. Remote-eligible roles covered.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.notes: Effective January 1, 2025 for employers with 15+ employees.

Chicago.name: Chicago
Chicago.notes: Chicago enacted earlier. Same pay range requirement.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.notes: Effective July 31, 2025 for employers with 25+ employees.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.notes: Effective June 1, 2024 for employers with 10+ employees.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.notes: Range required upon request AND must be provided proactively in job postings as of Oct 2021.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.notes: No state-level pay transparency law as of 2024. Federal rules apply. Monitor for Columbus/Cincinnati local ordinance activity.

at_will_exceptions.MT: Montana has just-cause termination protection — avoid language implying at-will status.
